features.summary: The System health page (/system-health; no demo page, docs/system-health-design.md) shows a server-computed verdict, a six-tile KPI row and seven tabs (Overview, API, Orders & suppliers, Queues & jobs, Alerts & incidents, Data stores, Integrity) over the 30 routes of map group health; the app shell shows a maintenance banner from the same health read. Every figure is a server-judged Measure; the console only polls (15 s / 30 s / 5 s while a run is going) and runs operator actions (maintenance, queue retry/pause, run job, integrity run, ack, rule CRUD/mute, incident declare/update/close) through confirm dialogs that show the server's problem+json. File paths without src/ are under src/features/system-health/.

endpoints.response: UI: polled every 15 s by the page (verdict, KPI 'Uptime 30 days' and 'Open alerts', Overview, Build card) AND by the app-shell maintenance banner on every admin page for system:read holders, deduped by React Query (staleTime 5 s, refetch on focus) (hooks/useHealth.ts:13-15, header/MaintenanceBanner.tsx:20) -> serve a snapshot the worker rebuilds every minute in the cache Redis + a live read of settings 'maintenance'. status: 'outage' when a core component is down, 'degraded' when any component is down/degraded or a critical alert is open, else 'operational'; never 'operational' while monitoring.status is 'unavailable' (send 'unknown' unless service_checks prove outage/degraded) (mocks/facts.ts:172-177, M216). since = start of the current status: earliest current problem (component since, open critical alert started_at); operational = last incident resolved_at or null; unknown = monitoring.lastScrapeAt (mocks/buildHealth.ts:100-121). checkedAt = snapshot time. monitoring = Prometheus reachability, detail text when not, lastScrapeAt of the API target. build = APP_VERSION as built (e.g. v1.42.0), 7-char GIT_SHA, APP_ENV, deploy time. components (service_checks, latest row per component): core keys api, postgres, redis, redis_queue, storage, workers, mail (kind core), 'supplier:<suppliers.id>' for EVERY supplier (disabled: status unknown, since null, lastCheckedAt null, detail 'checks are off'), 'gateway:<payment_gateways.id>'; latency = last latency_ms as Measure (thresholds per kind); uptime h24/d7/d30 = (checks not down)/checks x 100, value null without checks; detail = failure text only while failing. uptime = platform uptime (minutes with no core component down / minutes with checks) for 24h/7d/30d + daily = 30 UTC-day points oldest first, null for a day without checks. alerts (alert_events): open = Measure {value = firing + acknowledged count, unit count, warn 1, no crit/direction; state crit when any open critical (acknowledged included, M214), warn when any open, ok when none; {value null, state unknown} when rules could not be evaluated and nothing is open (M213)}; critical = open critical count incl. acknowledged; items = open alerts as AlertSummary, critical first then newest; trend = 96 x 15-min points of the open count over 24 h (from started_at/resolved_at). incidents = unresolved incidents newest first (IncidentSummary; components = component keys). maintenance = settings 'maintenance' (off: enabled false, the other five fields null).

Source service_checks aggregated with date_bin: bucketSeconds 60/300/1800/10800 for 1h/6h/24h/7d = 60/72/48/56 buckets, oldest first, the last one still filling (mocks/clock.ts:65-80). Bucket: status = worst check in it (down > degraded > ok), 'unknown' with no checks (worker restart, disabled supplier); checks = rows; failures = rows with status down; latencyMs = p95 of answered checks' latency_ms, null when none. Cache each (range, component) answer ~30 s: the all-components 7d read aggregates ~150k rows (index service_checks(component, checked_at)).

Series step = bucketSeconds 60/300/900/3600 for 1h/6h/24h/7d = 60/72/96/168 points per series, oldest first, null where no samples (gap). 'Now' Measures cover the last 5 min: requestsPerMin = sum(rate) x 60 (no thresholds: ok with a value, unknown when null); p50/p95/p99 in ms = histogram_quantile; rate4xx/rate5xx = share of 4xx/5xx answers in percent 0-100 (exclude 503 MAINTENANCE from rate5xx); count429 = 429 answers in the last 5 min. total = all surfaces (surface 'total', label 'All surfaces'); with ?surface= the whole answer is that surface: total = it, surfaces = [it], slowest = its endpoints (M215). slowest = at most 10 route templates (method, manifest path, surface) by p95 over the range, slowest first, requestsPerMin = average over the range. Every Measure carries unit, server state, warn/crit and direction (defaults mocks/thresholds.ts:12-21). KPI 'API p95'/'5xx rate' read total.p95/total.rate5xx + total.series (header/kpi.ts:54-70).

businessRules: The server judges every number: each figure is a Measure whose state comes from server-side thresholds; warn/crit are the limits applied, direction says which side is bad, value null => state unknown. The console never compares (types/common.ts:23-34; mocks/thresholds.ts:45-72).

No data is never healthy: while Prometheus is unavailable health is never 'operational' (map scenario system-alert step 5; M216); a figure without data is 'unknown', never 'ok' (mocks/thresholds.ts:45-47).
Overall status: 'outage' when a core component is down, 'degraded' when any component is down or degraded or a critical alert is open, else 'operational' (mocks/facts.ts:172-177).

A worker checks every minute: database, cache, storage, payment gateways and every supplier (accountinfo), writing status and latency to service_checks; uptime and outages derive from those rows, which are deleted after 90 days (scenario system-alert step 1; table service_checks).

Rules are evaluated every minute over their window; a breach creates one alert_events row (firing, severity, value, subject) unless the rule is muted (muted_until in the future) or switched off; e.g. supplier timeout rate > 20 % for 3 min -> critical alert on that supplier (scenario system-alert step 3; mocks/seedRules.ts).
Notifications: one message per rule channel (telegram, email), repeated only after the reminder interval until acknowledged (scenario system-alert step 4).

Acknowledge moves firing -> acknowledged only, records acknowledged_by/at + audit_logs and stops reminders; the alert stays open and an acknowledged critical alert still counts as critical (step 6; M214); otherwise 409 ALERT_ACKNOWLEDGED / ALERT_RESOLVED (mocks/routes/alerts.ts:35-51).
Only the server resolves alerts: after 3 consecutive ok minutes (resolved_at + a 'resolved' message); an acknowledged alert never closes earlier (step 10). There is no resolve endpoint.

Incidents: declaring starts the timeline at 'investigating' and links the alert (step 7); one incident per alert (mocks/routes/incidents.ts:53-58); every status change or update adds a server-written timeline line; closing needs rootCause (10+) and the optional update is the action taken (step 11; M205); a resolved incident is a record -> any PATCH 409 INCIDENT_CLOSED; incidents are never deleted (map ops LSCU).

Supplier pause (PATCH /admin/suppliers/:id status=paused) routes new orders to the next supplier by priority in service_supplier_links; orders already sent stay as they are (step 8); a paused supplier keeps its checks, a disabled one is unchecked (health 'unknown') (mocks/facts.ts:104-128).

Maintenance: the chosen scope answers 503 MAINTENANCE with the message and expected end; checkout maintenance creates no checkout session and holds nothing; the admin console and running merchant orders keep working; on/off/change are audited with the staff member; only PUT {enabled:false} ends it (scenario system-integrity steps 4, 5, 8; manifest PUT /admin/system/maintenance).

Ledger integrity: the nightly ledger_integrity job runs four read-only checks (entries sum to zero, account balance = sum of its lines, holds stuck > 24 h, confirmed payments without an entry) and stores the result in job_runs.result; a difference fires the critical ledger_mismatch rule naming the account and difference; corrections are reversing entries (POST /admin/clients/:id/wallet/adjust), never edits; a clean manual run resolves the alert (scenario system-integrity steps 1-3, 6-7).

Every scheduled or manual run writes job_runs (trigger schedule|manual|event; triggered_by for manual) (D020; manifest POST /admin/system/jobs/:name/run); one run per job at a time -> 409 JOB_ALREADY_RUNNING (mocks/routes/queues.ts:109-116, mocks/routes/integrity.ts:19-27); proposal: a reaper fails runs stuck in 'running' past a timeout so the guard cannot block forever.
Queue actions: pausing needs a reason (3+ chars) kept in audit_logs (M204); retry touches failed jobs only and answers how many moved (mocks/routes/queues.ts:34-87).
Every write of the group writes audit_logs with the staff member (manifest tables of every health write).

Permissions (manifest): system:read for every /admin/system read; system:manage for maintenance, retry, pause, run job and integrity run; alerts:read for alerts and rules, alerts:create/update/delete for rules, alerts:update for ack; incidents:read/create/update; suppliers:update for pause/resume. 403 detail names the missing permission (mocks/http.ts:44-46). Default roles: Owner and Admin manage; Finance, Support, Risk reviewer and Read only view (M198).

Database outage: reads that need live Postgres rows answer 503 DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE (mock: orders-health, integrity, integrity run; mocks/profile.ts:94), while health keeps answering from the snapshot and /database answers 200 status 'down' (M212).

Component keys are stable ids: fixed core keys incl. 'workers', plus 'supplier:<id>' and 'gateway:<id>'; incident components are validated against the known keys (422 'Unknown component', mocks/routes/incidents.ts:42-51); the declare prefill maps supplier alerts to 'supplier:<subjectId>' and queue alerts to 'workers' (tabs/alerts/incidents.ts:82-83).
Seed the rules the map scenarios need: supplier_timeout_rate (gt 20, 180 s, critical) and ledger_mismatch (gt 0, critical); the mock seeds ten rules with defaults worth copying (mocks/seedRules.ts).

Range: tabs send range=1h|6h|24h|7d (default 24h); the KPI row always reads metrics?range=24h, queues, orders-health and health (30-day uptime) whatever the page range (header/useKpis.ts:53-58; ASSUMED_CONTRACTS 'Health summary details').

Polling: health, alerts and queues every 15 s; other cards every 30 s; jobs and integrity every 5 s while a run is going; hidden tabs pause, focus refetches, answers younger than 5 s are reused, 5xx GETs are retried once (hooks/keys.ts:47; hooks/useHealthQuery.ts:26-45; src/lib/query/useApiQuery.ts:26-28). Serve health from a per-minute snapshot and checks/metrics/errors/database from ~15-30 s caches keyed by params.

questions.question: While Postgres is down, can the lists of GET .../database be null (not []) and locks.waiting / waitingClients null rather than 0? Should these two counts be Measures?

questions.question: When usage has no reading, are used and usedBytes zeros, last known values, or absent? Does Redis send maxBytes null or 0 without a limit?
questions.proposedAnswer: Send 0 with usage {value null, state unknown} (the console then omits the counts, M251). maxBytes null when maxmemory is 0; both Redis roles set maxmemory (D006).

questions.question: Over which window do a slow query's calls, meanMs and totalMs count, how many statements does slowQueries hold, and from which age is a transaction long?
questions.proposedAnswer: Since the last pg_stat_statements reset, done nightly by the data_retention job (about the last 24 h); top 10 by mean_exec_time with calls >= 20; a transaction is long when xact_start is older than 60 s (top 10 by duration, query truncated to 500 chars).

questions.question: Could GET /admin/system/integrity carry an overall result (or a count of failed checks), and the start time of a run that is going now?
questions.proposedAnswer: Yes, as extra fields: result ('pass'|'fail'|'unknown' = worst check of lastRun) and runningSince (started_at of the running run); keep lastRun = the last finished run.

questions.question: What is the ref format of an account finding, and can the ledger be filtered to one account? For entry and payment findings, is id the journal entry id and the payment id? How many findings per check?

A one-account ledger filter (accountId) belongs to Finance and can be added there.
